programme: RFX5 drives the RFX-CIITA enhanceosome that switches on the MHC class II locus (HLA-DMA/DMB/DOA/DOB/DPA1/DPB1/DQB2/DRA, plus CIITA itself and MHC-I genes HLA-E/HLA-F) for antigen presentation to CD4+ T cells; RORC is the canonical Th17 master regulator, sitting on IL23R, IL17A, IL17F, IL22, IL21, CCR6, FOXP3 and IL6/TNF/IL1R1 to commit those T cells to an IL-17/IL-23-axis fate; BACH2 acts downstream as a brake on that differentiation, repressing PRDM1 (BLIMP1) and regulating BCL2/TP53/XBP1/HMOX1 to restrain terminal effector commitment and hold the Th17/Treg (FOXP3) balance in check. Together these three describe an antigen-presentation-to-Th17-polarization-and-restraint axis, not a single physical complex.
role_in_a: In clear cell renal carcinoma this axis maps onto the tumor's well-documented immune-infiltrated phenotype: MHC class II upregulation by tumor and stromal cells (the RFX5/CIITA programme) and infiltration by IL-17-producing and Treg populations shaped by RORC/BACH2 activity are recurring features of the RCC immune microenvironment that underlie its responsiveness to checkpoint immunotherapy.
role_in_b: In psoriasis this axis is closer to textbook: RORC-driven Th17 cells producing IL-17A/F and IL-22 downstream of IL-23R signaling are the accepted proximal drivers of keratinocyte hyperproliferation, RFX5-dependent MHC-II presentation by dermal antigen-presenting cells is the upstream trigger for that T-cell activation, and BACH2 sets the threshold between regulatory and effector T-cell output in the skin-draining immune response.
shared_axis: Both tissue contexts are recognized, independently of each other, as sites where antigen presentation-driven Th17 polarization is a dominant immune programme rather than an incidental one — psoriasis as the prototypical IL-23/Th17 skin disease, ccRCC as an unusually immunogenic, immune-checkpoint-responsive tumor. The three factors would recur across patient subgroups in both diseases because the same MHC-II-to-Th17-to-homeostatic-brake circuitry is active in each, not because the diseases share a documented common cause.
reasoning: RFX5, RORC and BACH2 form a nameable and mechanistically real T-cell axis (MHC-II antigen presentation, Th17 commitment, and a homeostatic brake on effector differentiation), and each disease is separately understood in general immunology as being organized around exactly this kind of axis, which is what pushes the verdict to 'supported' rather than 'unexpected'. But nothing in the record placed in front of me actually shows this: Open Targets records no association for any of the three factors in either disease, the RORC hits retrieved for psoriasis are explicitly flagged as ambiguous, and the only concrete factual data are generic ReMap binding calls (RFX5 at 9/17 targets, BACH2 at 3/7) that confirm the factors occupy their canonical target genes but say nothing disease-specific. I deliberately did not build the story around the higher-recurrence factors (FOXD2 76/120, HOXB5 70/120, TBX6 68/120) because none of them cohere functionally with each other or with any retrieved evidence — recurrence rank and mechanistic coherence point to different factors here.
how_to_falsify: Take matched single-cell or multiplex-IHC data from ccRCC tumors and psoriatic skin lesions and test whether RORC+/IL-17A+ T-cell frequency correlates with RFX5/CIITA-driven MHC-II expression on the local antigen-presenting or tumor cell population in both tissues, and whether BACH2 expression in the same T cells inversely tracks with PRDM1 and terminal effector markers. If Th17 infiltration in ccRCC turns out to be independent of local MHC-II expression, or BACH2 shows no relationship to effector/Treg ratio in either tissue, the proposed circuit does not hold.
caveats: Kidney and skin are not anatomically or clinically linked tissues, so any shared axis has to be argued from convergent immunology rather than shared organ biology. The 120 patient-group comparisons come from only 4 independent cohort pairs, so the comparisons are not independent replicates and the apparent recurrence should be read cautiously. All three carrying factors sit in the lower half of the recurrence ranking (43-45%) rather than the top, and no tissue-generic exclusion list was provided for this pair to check against. The single-view exclusions (ING4, KAT8, VAX2, ARHGAP35, IRX2, NFE2L1, NR2E1, TFEC, DAXX, ZMYND8, JUN, ST18) do not overlap with the carrying factors, so the account is not resting on a one-subgroup artifact, but the absence of any disease-specific literature or Open Targets hit for RFX5, RORC or BACH2 means this account rests on general immunological plausibility, not on evidence retrieved for this pair.
